dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Have you ever eaten thịt chó? I see many Vietnamese people consider it a truyền thống dish.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Never! In Russia, dogs are friends, không food. But I see many thịt chó restaurants in Saigon. Have you tried it?

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Actually I also don't want to eat thịt chó. I think culture should change with time. But there's a secret - my grandfather really liked thịt chó dishes when he lived in Vietnam.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: That's interesting. In my homeland we also have foods that Westerners wouldn't understand. But thịt chó... I cannot. You know, I used to have a dog when I was little.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Maybe that's something we have in common. I also love dogs, but I respect truyền thống. Do you think eating thịt chó will disappear in Vietnam?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I'm không sure. Truyền thống are very difficult to change. But if you truly respect dogs as friends, how can you think about eating thịt chó?
